name: nconnect: fixed Kimi K3 vs Jev-assisted Auto, through Claude Code
research_question: Across these 50 tasks, how much money and time did Jev-assisted Auto save, and what happened to correctness?

B_rules.label: Pipeline check only: Auto with keyword rules (no decider)

left_at_default.NCONNECT_AUTO_EFFORT: unset (on: Auto raises reasoning effort on the first turn of a balanced or strong task)
left_at_default.NCONNECT_BACKGROUND_MODEL: unset (Claude Code's title and permission-classifier calls go to the catalog default, GLM 5.3 Flash, in both conditions)
left_at_default.NCONNECT_AUTO_DECIDER_TIMEOUT_MS: unset (2500 ms wait; the request may finish in the background for up to 20 s)

limits.max_model_requests_note: Counted as distinct assistant messages in Claude Code's stream (one per model call it makes). Claude Code 2.1.299 has no turn-limit flag, so the runner stops the session when the count is exceeded.

claude_code.notes: Reads and edits inside the workspace need no allow rule in acceptEdits mode. Subagents are disabled in both conditions: Claude Code would run them on its Haiku-tier model, which would break 'Kimi K3 for every foreground request' in condition A.

scoring.success: All hidden acceptance tests pass on the final workspace. Nothing else counts.
scoring.cost: Estimated. Provider-reported tokens per upstream request (recorder) times the prices in the manifest. Cached input is billed at the full input rate because Nebius publishes no cached-input price; a cache-free lower bound is reported alongside. Requests without reported usage are estimated from bytes and kept separate. Jev is charged per input token at its published rate.
scoring.duration: Wall time from launching nconnect to its exit, per task. Time to first visible output is the first non-empty text delta in Claude Code's stream.
scoring.failed_tasks: Included in every cost total. Cost per successful task divides total spend by successful tasks.
